decision.description: End of August 2026. The two signals known then: ONI Jul-Sep +2.16 (strong El Niño) and NASA POWER root-zone soil wetness 0.91 for 22-31 August, higher than in 84% of the past campaigns at this zone.

notes.text: Strongest El Niño signal at the end of August among the candidate campaigns (1981/82 to 2024/25): ONI Jul-Sep +1.79.

Largest share of planted soybean not harvested among the 2 strong El Niño campaigns (ONI Jul-Sep at or above +1.5): 5% (MAGyP planted against harvested area; the cause is not recorded). ONI Jul-Sep was +1.79.
Largest share of planted soybean not harvested at this department: 22% (MAGyP planted against harvested area; the cause is not recorded). It started with ONI Jul-Sep +0.54 (El Niño winter).
Worst maize yield on record at this department (1981/82 to 2024/25): 39% below its trend (observed, MAGyP). It started with an ONI Jul-Sep of -0.20 (neutral winter).

features: NOAA ONI Jul-Sep of the campaign start year

method.distance: Euclidean on z-scores; mean and sd from past campaigns only
method.candidates: campaigns 1981/82-2024/25 with observed or modeled yields for every crop
method.phase_rule: El Nino >= 0.5, strong >= 1.5, La Nina <= -0.5 on ONI Jul-Sep

signals.unit: ONI: degrees C anomaly; soil wetness: 0 to 1, no unit
signals.note: ONI Jul-Sep is one global index (NOAA, revised values). Soil wetness is the NASA POWER mean of 22-31 August at the department head town, a cell of about 55 km.

yields.note: MAGyP department Balcarce, Buenos Aires. 2 of 88 values are modeled from NASA POWER because MAGyP has none; each campaign gives the provenance of its two values.

backtest.text: Backtest of this method (307 campaigns, 10 zones, k = 7): analogs chosen by ONI Jul-Sep plus soil wetness predicted the margin no better than averaging all earlier campaigns (mean absolute error 123.2 against 122.3 USD/ha), and better than k random campaigns (p = 0.007). The analogs are real named cases, not a forecast.

margins_meta.note: Gross margin of one campaign on own land: department yield of each analog campaign, today's A3 harvest futures and today's MAGyP regional costs. A scenario, not a forecast.

margin_assumptions: Yield = MAGyP regional model yield x (1 + the department's yield anomaly against its linear trend in that campaign; observed from MAGyP, or modeled from NASA POWER where MAGyP has no value).
Costs, rent and structure are today's MAGyP regional values, applied to every past campaign.
Harvest and marketing cost is the same share of gross income as in the MAGyP table.
Price = A3 harvest-contract settlement today x the delivery/planting ratio of a past campaign; price and yield independent (Argentina is a price taker).
Previous-crop effect: only first-crop soybean after maize, cited +7% (used here) up to +10%; every other previous-crop effect is 0.
Not included: soil, weed and disease effects of monoculture over years; excess-water losses beyond those already in observed yields.
Department-to-MAGyP-region assignment by geography (MAGyP does not publish it).

Cover crop: direct cost only (60, 80 used, 86 USD/ha; cited, old nominal USD), no extra rent; soybean yield effect 0 (the INTA Pergamino trial found no difference). Soil benefits are not computed in this case.
Costs, rent and cost structure: MAGyP Sudeste Buenos Aires region, report 2026-09.
Prices: A3 harvest-contract settlements of 2026-11-13 (soybean SOJ.ROS/MAY27, maize MAI.ROS/ABR27, wheat TRI.ROS/ENE27); reference only, raw prices are not redistributed.
compare.risk_note: Secondary, with small n. Each strategy is run over 7 analog campaigns x 14 price campaigns = 98 scenarios. A price campaign is the ratio of the delivery-month to the planting-months settlement of the same A3 contract in a past year; only years where soybean, maize and wheat all have a ratio are used. This is not a distribution of the coming campaign: read the named analog campaigns first.

unharvested_meta.note: MAGyP planted against harvested area, campaigns 1981/82 to 2024/25 grouped by the ONI Jul-Sep phase. Soybean is MAGyP 'soja total'. Campaigns with no planted area are skipped; the cause of the loss is not recorded.

not_computed.reason: No team model computes it for this zone.
No soil carbon model has been run for any rotation of this case.
No nitrogen balance or nitrate loss is modeled; fertilizer enters the margin only as a MAGyP cost.
No model of pests, diseases or weeds under each rotation; the margin compares single campaigns.
Yields are department anomalies (MAGyP, or a NASA POWER model where MAGyP has none), not field measurements.

limits.title: Analog years are not a forecast
limits.text: In a backtest over 307 campaigns in the 10 zones (target campaigns 1991/92 to 2024/25, k = 7), picking analogs by ONI Jul-Sep and soil wetness predicted margins no better than the average of every earlier campaign: mean absolute error 123.2 against 122.3 USD/ha (-0.7%). It did beat k random campaigns (p = 0.007). The signal showed up in Marcos Juarez and Rio Cuarto only. Use the analogs as real named cases, not as a forecast.

limits.title: No better rotation policy was found
limits.text: Two team experiments looked for a rule that adapts the rotation year by year and found none. A tabular decision model (dynamic programming) earned -3 [-8; +3] USD/ha/year against the best fixed rotation (95% interval) and passed no criterion in 0 of 10 zones; Q-learning matched it in 85 to 100% of states. In the Pergamino lab the best policy gained +32 [12; 49] USD/ha/year against a pre-registered threshold of 56, and a one-step greedy rule equals the dynamic program. So no rotation is presented as the winner.

limits.title: 2026/27 is outside the historical range
limits.text: ONI Jul-Sep 2026 is +2.16, above every candidate campaign (highest: +1.79 in 1997/98). The analogs are the closest campaigns available, not equivalents, and a campaign this strong cannot be backtested.

limits.title: ONI Jul-Sep is not strictly known on 31 August
limits.text: NOAA publishes ONI Jul-Sep in early October, and the file used here holds revised values, not the ones published at the time. The strictly known alternative on 31 August is May-Jun-Jul.

limits.title: NASA POWER describes the zone, not the field
limits.text: Each value covers a cell of about 55 km around the head town of the department. Root-zone soil wetness (GWETROOT) is a model estimate, not measured soil water.

limits.title: Margins are scenarios
limits.text: One campaign, today's A3 harvest futures and today's MAGyP costs, applied to the department yield anomaly of each past campaign. Multi-year effects of each rotation on soil, weeds and diseases are left out, and excess-water losses count only where they are already in the observed yields.

limits.title: Wheat does not respond to these signals
limits.text: In the team's yield model, NASA POWER climate cuts the leave-one-year-out error against the trend by 19.1% for maize and 15.9% for soybean, but by -0.6% for wheat, which is nothing. The signals say little about the strategy with wheat.

limits.title: Management has changed since the old campaigns
limits.text: Defensive practices and forecasts have improved, so old campaigns resemble today less. Measuring each yield against its own trend corrects only part of it.

limits.title: Some yield anomalies are modeled
limits.text: 2 of the 88 maize and soybean yield anomalies of this zone come from a NASA POWER climate model because MAGyP has no value. Validated leaving one year out, it cuts the error against the trend by 15.9% for soybean and 19.1% for maize. Each campaign says which of the two it is.

glossary.definition: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index, (near-infrared - red) / (near-infrared + red) from satellite reflectance. It has no unit; higher means greener, denser vegetation.

NASA POWER's modeled wetness of the root zone, a number from 0 to 1 with no unit. It is a model estimate for a cell of about 55 km, not millimetres of plant-available water and not a field measurement.

Oceanic Nino Index: the three-month mean sea-surface temperature anomaly in the Nino 3.4 region of the Pacific, from NOAA. This case uses the July-September value. At or above +0.5 is El Niño (+1.5 or more is called strong here), at or below -0.5 is La Niña.
Potential crop evapotranspiration minus the actual one in the daily water balance, in mm: the water the crop would have used if the soil had supplied it (FAO-56). It is not a yield loss.
Water that exceeded what the modeled soil profile can hold and left it as drainage or runoff, in mm. It is not flooding or waterlogging.
Daily accounting of rain and evapotranspiration against the water a soil profile can store, following FAO-56. Here it is a bucket model run on NASA POWER weather.
A real past campaign, such as 1997/98, whose two signals at the end of August (ONI Jul-Sep and soil wetness) were among the closest to this year's. It is a named case, not a forecast.
A department yield compared with its own linear trend over 1981-2024, in percent. Observed means it comes from MAGyP; modeled means MAGyP has no value and a NASA POWER climate model fills it.

glossary.term: Gross margin and gross margin after rent
glossary.definition: Gross margin is yield x price minus harvest and marketing costs and direct costs, in USD per hectare, following the MAGyP method. After rent also subtracts the regional rent per hectare, which matters on rented land.
